senses.gloss: ch. same, to stir up, awaken; to awake.
units: Targ. Job XLI, 2 יְעוּרִ׳ (ed. Lag. a. oth. יְעִרִ׳ Af.).—

<cite ref="Taanit 4a:1">Taan. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>עוּרוּ</he>, v. <cite ref="P00361"><he>עוּרְפִּילָא</he></cite>.—Part. <cite ref="P00520"><he>עָיֵיר</he></cite>, <cite ref="P00672"><he>עָיֵר</he></cite>; f. <cite ref="P00521"><he>עָיְירָא</he></cite>, <cite ref="P00932"><he>עָיְרָא</he></cite>.
Targ. Cant. V, 2.—Part. pass. עִיר, pl. עִירִין, עִירֵי awake.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1:28">Y. Ber. I, 2ᵈ</cite> <he>עד כדון ברייתא ע׳</he> until then (the end of the first night-watch) men are awake.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 29b:3">Snh. 29ᵇ</cite> <he>ע׳ ושכבי ליהוי וכ׳</he> shall those awake and those asleep be witnesses against thee (i.e. wouldst thou say so within the hearing of &c.)?
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 14:9">Targ. Is. XIV, 9</cite> <he>אֲעִירַת</he> (ed. Lag. <he>אעדת</he>, read <he>אֲעָרַת</he>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Zechariah 4:1">Targ. Zech. IV, 1</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Deuteronomy 32:11">Targ. Y. II, Deut. XXXII, 11</cite> (not <he>מֵעִיד</he>); a. e.—

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 22:6">Midr. Till. to Ps. XXII</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 57:9">ib. LVII, 9</cite>) <he>אֲעִיר יקרי וכ׳</he> wake up, my dignity (soul), before the dignity of my Maker (v. infra).

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 80:3">Targ. Ps. LXXX, 3</cite>. Targ. Y. I Deut. l. c.—Y. Ber. I, 2ᵈ (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 57:9">Ps. LVII, 9</cite>) <he>אנא הוינא מְעוֹרֵר שחרה וכ׳</he> I am wont to wake up the dawn, the dawn never wakes me up; Pesik. Vayhi, p. 63ᵃ; <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 17:1">Pesik. R. s. 17</cite> <he>ושחרה לא עוֹרְרַתְנִי</he>; Midr. Till. l. c.; <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 2:22">Lam. R. to II, 18</cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: , Ittaf. אִתָּעַר to be stirred up; to awake; to bestir one’s self.
units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 14:12">Targ. Job XIV, 12</cite>.

<cite ref="Habakkuk 2:19">Hab. II, 19</cite>; a. e.—Y. Ber. l. c. <he>אִתְעִיר יקרי</he> wake up, my dignity (v. supra); Pesik. l. c. <he>אִיתְּעַר</he>; Pesik. R. l. c.; Lam. R. l. c.; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 776:1">Yalk. Ps. 776</cite> <he>יִתָּעַר יקרי וכ׳</he> let my dignity wake up.

<cite ref="Berakhot 4a:5">Ber. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>לאִתְעוּרֵי משנתיה</he> (Ms. M. <he>לאִתְעוּרֵיה</he>) for the purpose of (his) being waked up from his sleep; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 186">Yalk. Ex. 186</cite>.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 12">Lev. R. s. 12</cite>, beg. <he>א׳ משנתיה וכ׳</he> when he woke up from his sleep, he saw &c.; a. fr.—

Koh. R. to I, 8 כיון דא׳ בך חמרא וכ׳ since that wicked man’s ass has been stirred up against thee (as it will be a constant reproach to thee that that man has caused thee to ride on the Sabbath), thou canst no longer stay &c.; [Matt. K.: since that wicked man’s ass has brayed at thee, as if from נער, v. נָעַר I.]
